articles.summary: Sweet, tart and ridiculously easy to make, Ina Garten’s chunky cranberry conserve proves storebought can be spectacular. body: Thanksgiving is just around the corner, and if you’re still staring down a long list of dishes to prepare, Ina Garten has a little shortcut for you. Her secret to a delicious, homemade-tasting cranberry sauce: start with a can.

In her new cookbook, Simply Ina, the Barefoot Contessa shares her clever trick for turning store-bought sauce into something special in 20 mins. Garten simmers it with a grated granny smith apple, fresh orange juice and orange zest. The fruit adds brightness and a little tartness, while raisins and chopped pecans stirred in at the end lend sweetness and crunch.

Recipe edited from Simply Ina, by Ina Garten, published by Clarkson Potter, an imprint of the Crown Publishing Group, a division of Penguin Random House LLC. To order a copy, visit guardianbookshop.com.

articles.title: 2026 Was the Year Restaurants Went Full Midwest
articles.summary: This is an excerpt from Pre Shift, our newsletter for bartenders, restaurant workers and the hospitality industry. Subscribe for more perspectives like this in your inbox.
body: At Kyle Knall’s Milwaukee restaurant Cassis, the showstopper dish is ravioli Dauphiné, a sheet of 24 tiny squares stuffed with the Wisconsin cheese Pleasant Ridge Reserve. Topped with glazed seasonal veggies, kernels of sweet corn in summer and sliced honeynut squash in late fall, it speaks to Knall’s Midwestern-meets-French approach—one of the reasons why his restaurant earned a slot on Eater’s 2026 list of the Best New Restaurants in America.

That welcoming community sensibility is a key component of Midwestern restaurants. Knall counts several farmers and shoppers at the West Allis Farmers Market, where he sources for Cassis, as some of his regulars. “To me, it shows that’s really what Midwest food is: supporting those communities,” he says.

Perhaps more than anything, it’s hospitality that sets these spots apart. “Hospitality is our biggest focus between both restaurants and maybe even more of a focus than the food,” Knall says. “To me, the way that our team makes you feel in the restaurants is such a Midwest thing.” And at Cordelia, where the slogan is “Midwest Nice,” Cimino says: “It’s welcoming you into our proverbial home.”

articles.title: 20+ Best Sweatpants for Relaxed (Yet Refined) Lounging
articles.summary: Every wardrobe deserves to include a pair of the best sweatpants for women. Shop cotton, cashmere, and wide-leg options from Nike, Vuori, Toteme, and more.
body: All products featured on Vogue are independently selected by our editors. However, we may earn affiliate revenue on this article and commission when you buy something.

Despite their reputation for being informal, sweatpants occupy a plum position within our wardrobes. A pillar in travel uniforms and off-duty outfit rotations, this MVP athleisure staple has come quite a long way since its gym wear associations. And for those pairs crafted in luxurious materials and in modern silhouettes, sweatpants can even replace denim or trousers when styled well.

The season’s best sweatpants run the spectrum of fabrication and design. On the traditional side, activewear labels from Nike to Adidas offer classic joggers cut from cotton. Contemporary cult-favorite labels like Jamie Haller, Lisa Yang, and Attersee have masterfully reimagined the sweatpant for a modern wardrobe (Haller’s pintuck pants would look fabulous with a thin turtleneck and check blazer layered on top). And, of course, luxury labels like The Row have always set the bar for the perfect pull-on pant.

articles.title: 11 Best Lab-Grown Diamonds 2026: Fine Jewelry to Engagement Rings
articles.summary: Discover the best lab-grown diamonds from brands like Brilliant Earth, Grown Brilliance, Pandora, Dorsey & more so you can sparkle sustainably.
body: “Lab-grown diamonds are the great equalizer,” says Jean Dousset, the great-grandson of Louis Cartier who pivoted his namesake label to exclusively lab-grown stones in 2023. “People don’t have to compromise anymore to own something exceptional.” Once considered the understudy to mined diamonds, these stones (and therefor, the best ​lab-grown diamond brands), have officially taken center stage—and they’re not just performing, they’re dazzling. Lab-grown diamonds are real diamonds. Not simulants, not stand-ins. We’re talking pure carbon, identical in chemical, physical, and optical makeup to what’s been pulled from the earth for centuries—just made in a lab, not dug up from a mine.
That sentiment is echoed by a growing number of designers (and their clients) who love that you can go bigger, bolder, and cleaner—ethically and aesthetically—without inflating the price tag.

articles.title: 6 Jewel-Toned Outfits to Wear to Every Holiday Party This Season
articles.summary: From glittering gold and shimmering silver to rich burgundy and royal purple, here’s how to style jewel-toned outfits for every festive occasion on your calendar.
body: Everyday opulence, ornate pieces with a Midas touch—however you choose to describe the fall/winter 2026 trend that’s taken over our feeds and carts, it’s now reaching its peak just in time for holiday dressing. And while lavish textures, from floral brocade to lustrous velvet and satin, are key to nailing the trend, they aren’t the only entry point. This party season, we’re opening up a jewel box of glittering gold, rich burgundy, and royal purple and embracing a more colorful approach to festive dressing.
Shine bright in these jewel-toned outfits—all put together for a memorable holiday night out.

Go for fashion gold this holiday season with Magda Butrym’s gold lamé jacket and Zara’s black tuxedo pants, complete with a built-in cummerbund. Pair the dazzling duo with The Row’s peep-toe heels and Savette’s pearl-encrusted pouch bag. For an extra dose of opulence, pin Juju Vera’s gold shoulder dusters in your ears and a pretty floral brooch on your jacket.
